newsitem.title: UK: U.S. STOCKS EDGE HIGHER IN LONDON TRADING.
newsitem.headline: U.S. STOCKS EDGE HIGHER IN LONDON TRADING.

text.p: U.S. stocks were marked slightly higher in London trading on Friday, extending yesterday's New York gains amid hopes for benign U.S. consumer prices and retail sales figures due before Wall Street opens, traders said.

"We are looking slightly higher," said a trader at one U.S. securities house here. "Famous last words but the numbers are expected to be friendly, I'd expect the Dow to be between five and eight points higher at the open."
Yet, with the Dow bumping up against record high levels, traders said further gains could be limited in the run-up to an expected interest rate rise by the Federal Reserve.

"The market is likely to remain nervous until we get a Fed tightening, whenever that will be," said another trader in U.S. stocks. "But if there is only a quarter-point rate rise, it won't have much effect on the corporate profits outlook."
Today's August consumer price report is expected to show a 0.2 percent month-on-month increased to give a 2.9 percent annual increase.
Retail prices also due at 1230 GMT are expected to show a 0.7 percent increase, or 0.4 percent excluding autos.
The 30-year T-bond was slightly higher, up 1/32 at 96-00, while S&P 500 December futures were up 0.05 points at 678.15.
Among individual stocks, Oracle Corp recovered from an initial after-hours decline following first-quarter earnings little different from analyst expectations.

Traders said the stock was quoted up 1/4 at 37-3/4, buoyed by a confident statement from the software company that said license sales rose 27 percent, while revenues from services such as training, consulting and support expanded 45 percent.
Ford Motor Co was up 3/8 at 32 after a report in the Wall Street Journal said the company was close to a labour agreement seen as positive for its profits outlook.
General Motors Corp was down 1/8 at 48-1/8.
W.R. Grace & Co was marked 1 higher at 72-1/4 after a report that the company could be a takeover target, traders said.
Yeterday the Dow closed 17.02 points higher at 5,771.94, just short of the record 5,778.00 set in May.
Stocks and bonds were buoyed by tame wholesale inflation report, cooling fears that the Federal Reserve will hike rates to ward off inflation risks even before its September 24 policy meeting.
